text: Which wills and estates law firms in Logan and Western Corridor (Ipswich to Brisbane) specialise in contesting a will, Family Provision Applications (FPA), and estate litigation?

sections.text:
Several firms advertise relevant expertise across Logan, Ipswich and Brisbane’s western corridor:

| Firm | Relevant locations or coverage | Relevant expertise |
|---|---|---|
| **Turner Freeman Lawyers** | Logan, Ipswich and Brisbane | Contested wills, will-validity disputes, Family Provision claims, estate litigation and executor advice.[1][2] |
| **The Estate Lawyers** | Queensland-wide; Brisbane office | Specialist Queensland practice focused solely on wills and estates, including contested wills, FPAs, executor disputes, inheritance defence and estate litigation.[5] |
| **Armstrong Legal** | Ipswich and Queensland-wide | Contests, challenges and defences of wills; FPAs; undue influence, testamentary capacity, fraud, executor removal and other estate disputes.[4] |
| **Walker Pender** | Ipswich office | Will disputes, Family Provision claims under Queensland’s Succession Act, negotiation and Supreme Court representation.[9] |
| **SKC Lawyers** | Logan | Contested wills, probate disputes, asset disputes, estate litigation, mediation and court proceedings.[6] |
| **Wills & Estate Lawyers Brisbane** | Brisbane, Logan and Ipswich coverage | Contested wills, FPAs, executor disputes, will interpretation and estate litigation; the firm advertises no-win-no-fee arrangements for will disputes and FPAs.[3] |
| **Thynne + Macartney** | Brisbane | Estate litigation, FPAs and dispute resolution; the firm identifies accredited succession-law expertise and recognition for wills-and-estates litigation.[8] |
| **Go To Court Lawyers** | Logan and Ipswich | Will challenges, further-provision claims, preparation of court documents, negotiation and representation in contested estate proceedings.[7][10] |

**Most specialist-looking options:** The Estate Lawyers, Armstrong Legal and Thynne + Macartney appear particularly focused on contested estates or succession litigation. For a nearby office, Turner Freeman has explicit Logan and Ipswich coverage, while Walker Pender has an Ipswich office.

In Queensland, an FPA generally requires notice to the executor within **six months of death** and filing within **nine months of death**, according to the cited Logan guidance.[2] These deadlines can be decisive, so obtain advice promptly and ask each firm about eligibility, prospects, funding, mediation strategy and whether it regularly appears in the Supreme Court of Queensland.
